author: philly leader
title: Eagles players participate in Thanksgiving volunteer activities across Philadelphia
text:
Jaelan Phillips, who recently joined the Philadelphia Eagles, has begun contributing to the local community through volunteer work. Ahead of Thanksgiving, Phillips and his fiancé volunteered at Philabundance in South Philadelphia, assisting with sorting food drive donations.
Philabundance aims to address hunger in the region. Lauren Webb, Chief Food Sourcing Officer at Philabundance, said, “It’s really exciting for our staff, our volunteers, to see Jaelan joining the efforts and putting his all behind helping the community. We’re excited to have him here.”
Phillips emphasized the importance of using his position as an NFL athlete to help others. “It’s incredible to be able to come here,” he said. “Obviously, as NFL athletes, we have an incredible platform to make a difference. Then Philadelphia, being so passionate about the Eagles, so passionate about the community, being able to come here and package food. Right now, the way the country’s going, there’s a lot of food insecurity, a lot of need. To be able to come here and help out doing this is really amazing.”
He also discussed his ongoing commitment to service through his foundation focused on youth empowerment via music education and sports programs. Previously recognized for his charitable work with the Miami Dolphins—including participating in cancer fundraising events and supporting marginalized communities—Phillips continues these efforts in Philadelphia.
“We have this big platform to be able to make a difference,” Phillips said. “So, I think that it’s kind of our responsibility to lead [by] example and to inspire other people to give back as well. I’ve always loved it. I grew up doing community service, so being in the league, being able to do it more, has been a great privilege.”
Other Eagles players also took part in holiday initiatives using funds from a $250,000 donation provided by Amazon for their participation in a Black Friday game. Activities included meal distributions at organizations such as Boys and Girls Club Philadelphia (with Quinyon Mitchell, Fred Johnson, and Joshua Uche), ACME Markets Foundation (Saquon Barkley), Love Pray Peace Project (Tyler Steen), Salvation Army (Jordan Davis), Chester Community Distribution and Kipp School (Nakobe Dean), and additional support for families by Jalyx Hunt.
Eagles rookies distributed 100 Thanksgiving meals at Parkside Association of Philadelphia with Silvi Materials.
